objective_checks.detail: changing docs/guide.md routes as expected across 3 workflow(s)
changing src/index.js routes as expected across 3 workflow(s)
changing README.md, LICENSE routes as expected across 3 workflow(s)
required check(s) always fire and gate internally (.github/workflows/tests.yml)
event-only workflows carry no path filters (.github/workflows/nightly-sweep.yml, .github/workflows/triage.yml)

dimensions.name: Completeness
dimensions.rationale: All three pull_request/push workflows (deploy, docs-site, tests) received deliberate decisions, the schedule/issue workflows were correctly identified as having no path-trigger to scope, and the required check was handled with always-run job-level skipping rather than a workflow path filter — exactly the semantics needed to avoid a strict-required-check deadlock.

dimensions.name: Salience
dimensions.rationale: Each list maps to what the workflow actually consumes (its sources, configs, and its own file) rather than a catch-all or sibling copy, but the filters key on package.json while both deploy and the tests-skip logic run npm ci, so a lockfile-only change would wrongly be treated as irrelevant.

dimensions.name: Restraint
dimensions.rationale: The agent left the schedule-only and issue-driven workflows untouched, deliberately reasoned around the branch-protection ruleset instead of editing it, and confined its diff to only the three workflow files the audit called for.
